extracted.intended_audience: Editors of American Mathematical Society journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for editors of American Mathematical Society journals on managing submissions, refereeing, author communication, timeliness, and ethical conduct to guide decision-making and maintain editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission will be acknowledged within a short period of time. The acknowledgement will provide the author with an expected time for an update on the paper's status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors usually will make arrangements for acknowledgement when they are traveling or unable to send acknowledgement themselves. A prompt acknowledgement should include an expected timeline for the next status update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely declination of clearly unsuitable submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that are judged unsuitable for publication without being refereed will be declined in a timely fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should promptly identify and decline papers that do not merit peer review to respect authors' time and keep the editorial process efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee deadline agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each referee who agrees to review a manuscript will be asked to agree also to a target date for completion of a report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inviting referees, editors should obtain a specific target completion date to manage expectations and scheduling of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up with referees near target date
rubrics_metrics.description: An editor will write to the referee near the target date for a report in order to ask for a new target date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should proactively follow up with referees approaching or past their agreed deadline to request a revised date and keep the review progressing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge receipt of referee reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Every referee's report will be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must communicate to referees that their reports have been received, closing the loop and maintaining professional courtesy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for replacing referees and restarting review
rubrics_metrics.description: An editor (or group of editors) will have a specific procedure to decide when to choose an alternative referee in order to restart the refereeing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should have a clear process for identifying when to seek alternate reviewers, and must write to the author when the refereeing process is restarted, providing a new expected time for an update on the paper's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate and offer withdrawal option after prolonged delay
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decision has not been made 12 months after submission, the editor will write to the author to explain the reasons for delay and to offer the option of withdrawing the paper from the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with best efforts, decisions may take long; editors are required to proactively explain delays at the 12-month mark and present the author the option to withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain regular contact and efficient editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of these guidelines is to ensure that the editorial process for AMS journals is carried out as efficiently as possible and that editors maintain regular contact with authors during this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should prioritize timely communications and efficient handling of submissions so authors are kept informed throughout the editorial lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Society ethical guidelines and professional courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors for journals of the American Mathematical Society are expected to follow the Society's ethical guidelines, treating all potential authors with reasonable professional courtesy, responding promptly to submissions and making decisions based on the merit of the paper as well as its suitability to the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must base decisions on merit and suitability, respond promptly, and treat authors respectfully. While editors are not obliged to provide a rationale for not accepting a paper or a detailed list of errors and corrections, when information is available that would help an author improve a paper, the editor should communicate that information to the author if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of the American Mathematical Society are managed by editors who are appointed by the Society, but who carry out their responsibilities with much independence. The Society values the editorial independence of its journals and their editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should exercise independent judgment in editorial decisions while following the Society's endorsed guidelines to ensure fairness and institutional reputation.
